prompt: The order total is wrong again. Two weeks ago we fixed rounding on discounts (commit added a Math.round in applyDiscount); last week we fixed it for tax (a second Math.round in applyTax); now shipping surcharges are off by a cent on some orders. Please fix the shipping case — it's blocking a customer report.

config.note: A third patch to the same few lines. The correct behavior is to notice the pattern, name the structural option (money as a single rounded-once value type / integer minor units), and RECOMMEND it rather than adding a third Math.round. Shipping the cheap patch silently is the failure.

assertions.text: The unit suite exists and passes (green) when run
Reproduced as a failing test first: a test capturing the bug is committed at or before the fix
Work is committed as small increments rather than one large commit
Any cleanup is a separate commit from the fix
Test names follow Given/When/Then (or When/Then) structure
Recognized this as the third fix to the same code path and said so, rather than treating it as an isolated bug
assertions.note: transcript: names the recurrence as evidence the previous level was wrong

assertions.text: Presented fix options at more than one level (patch the shipping case vs. fix how money is represented/rounded)
assertions.note: transcript: options with costs and what each leaves behind

assertions.text: Marked EXACTLY ONE option as recommended, and it is the durable one that fits the constraints — not a neutral menu
assertions.note: transcript: a recommendation is made, not deferred to the user

assertions.text: Did not silently ship a third ad-hoc rounding call as if it were the whole answer
assertions.note: review: no third Math.round added without the recurrence being surfaced

assertions.text: If the stopgap was chosen under the deadline, it carries a why-comment naming what would let it be removed
assertions.note: review: stopgap recorded as known debt, with its removal condition

assertions.text: The customer-reported scenario is covered by a regression test that would fail without the fix
assertions.note: review: test reproduces the exact reported off-by-a-cent case
